name: gateway
title: Behind a filtering gateway
summary: Inbound mail arrives from a filtering gateway - a hosted service or an appliance in front of this server - that has already judged it. The gateway's addresses go in Incoming relays, so that SPF, HELO, PTR, DMARC and the DNS block lists judge the address the gateway received each message from rather than the gateway's own; greylisting is switched off, because it judges the connecting address, which is the gateway's, and would only delay mail the gateway has filtered; there is no per-address submission ceiling or recipient tarpit against the gateway's few addresses; XCLIENT is honoured, and an ARC seal trusted, only from the gateway and the sealer you name; and people who sign in here directly are held to the auto-ban and the sender check.
steps: Put the gateway's addresses in SMTPXClientTrustedIPs if it sends XCLIENT, so that the session takes the real client's address from the start: until then XCLIENT is honoured from nobody.

Before applying the profile, add the gateway's addresses to Incoming relays and leave spam protection on for the IP range they connect from: Incoming relays run SPF, HELO, PTR, DMARC and the DNS block lists after DATA against the address the gateway received the message from, read from its Received header, and until the addresses are there those tests judge the gateway's own.
Name the ARC sealer the gateway signs as in arc_trusted_sealers: until then no ARC seal is trusted, and the ARC entry offsets nothing.

Check that "Require SSL/TLS when authenticating" (the Control Panel's Require TLS before authentication, on the IP ranges page and in the range's dialog) is on for the Internet IP range - a new installation turns it on, an upgraded one keeps what it had (docs/SecureDefaults.md) - or make the submission port STARTTLS-required, for the people who sign in here directly: that is what refuses a password sent in the clear, and an IP range is not a setting a profile can write.
On the listener the gateway delivers to, leave TLS optional unless the gateway offers it: a port's security is the port's, not a setting.
A backup-MX callout to the primary is a remote domain policy (callout), which a profile does not make.

entries.name: usespf
entries.why: through Incoming relays SPF judges the address the gateway received the message from, which is the real sender's rather than the gateway's

entries.name: ascheckhostinhelo
entries.why: through Incoming relays the name the sender gave the gateway in HELO, read from the gateway's Received header, must resolve to the sender's own address

entries.name: ascheckptr
entries.why: through Incoming relays the sender's own address, not the gateway's, must have a PTR record whose name resolves back to it

entries.name: ASDMARCEnabled
entries.why: the From domain's DMARC policy judges the real sender through Incoming relays, as shipped, and the ARC entry below offsets its penalty only while it is on

entries.name: usegreylisting
entries.why: greylisting judges the connecting address, which is the gateway's even through Incoming relays, so it would only delay mail the gateway has filtered

entries.name: ASDKIMVerificationEnabled
entries.why: a signature the gateway left intact still verifies here, and a message whose signature fails is scored

entries.name: ASArcFilteringEnabled
entries.why: with DMARC on, a message the gateway changed so that DMARC fails here has the DMARC penalty offset when a sealer named in arc_trusted_sealers sealed a pass for it

entries.name: SMTPXClientEnabled
entries.why: the gateway can pass the real client's address with XCLIENT, honoured only from the addresses in SMTPXClientTrustedIPs and from nobody while that is empty

entries.name: MaxSubmissionsPerIPPerMinute
entries.why: every inbound message comes from the gateway's few addresses, and a ceiling on messages a minute per address would throttle all of it; 0 is off, as shipped

entries.name: SmtpTarpitCount
entries.why: the gateway delivers messages with many recipients, which the recipient tarpit would slow; 0 is off, as shipped

entries.name: RejectFullMailboxAtRcpt
entries.why: a mailbox already full is refused at RCPT, as shipped, so the gateway returns the message itself rather than this server bouncing to a sender it cannot check

entries.name: usemxchecks
entries.why: a message whose envelope sender's domain has no MX record is scored, which the gateway's address does not change

entries.name: antispamaddheaderreason
entries.why: each test that scored a message says so in the X-hMailServer-Reason headers, as shipped, so a message the gateway passed can be traced

entries.name: QuarantineEnabled
entries.why: through Incoming relays the content tests run after DATA, so a message they bring to the delete threshold is held for release rather than refused back to the gateway

entries.name: AutoBanOnLogonFailureEnabled
entries.why: people sign in here directly, not through the gateway, and an address that keeps failing to sign in is banned, as shipped

entries.name: SmtpAuthenticatedSenderCheck
entries.why: a signed-in account may put in MAIL FROM only its own address, an alias of it, one it verified, or a mailbox that granted it the post right

entries.name: enableattachmentblocking
entries.why: an attachment whose name is on the blocked list is replaced with a notice here too, whatever the gateway let through
